method: Read official versioned primary documentation/source using web tools. No broker, JVM, runtime or performance experiment performed. Citations remain only in audit.

sources.title: Kafka 4.0 producer reliability
sources.verification: acks=all waits for current ISR; idempotence requires compatible acks/retries/in-flight settings. Bounded producer buffer and delivery timeout are separate from downstream business completion.

sources.title: Kafka 4.0 design and exactly-once
sources.verification: Kafka transactions atomically bind Kafka output and input positions; external sinks require cooperation. SSL disables sendfile in the documented implementation. Retained page-cache, batching and compression mechanisms; no universal throughput result asserted.

sources.title: Kafka 4.0 consumer protocol
sources.verification: New consumer protocol is client opt-in with group.protocol=consumer; session/heartbeat controls move to broker configuration. Classic-client tuning must not be copied unconditionally.

sources.title: Kafka 4.0 eligible leaders
sources.verification: ELR is disabled by default in 4.0; it adds eligible candidates after ISR selection and is not equivalent to unclean election.

sources.title: RabbitMQ 4.3 confirms
sources.verification: Publisher confirms and consumer ACKs are independent. Mandatory unroutable Return precedes confirmation. Durable persistent confirmation concerns disk persistence; quorum confirmation concerns accepted majority. Delivery tags are channel-scoped; multi-ACK must not cross unfinished work.

sources.title: RabbitMQ 4.3 quorum
sources.verification: Verified majority availability, strict 0–31 priority levels since 4.3, delivery/acquired-count distinction, nack versus reject failure accounting, global QoS rejection, and reliable dead-letter prerequisites. Queue membership is distinct from cluster node count. Retained version-specific claims.

sources.title: RabbitMQ 4.3 TTL
sources.verification: Per-message expiry and queue expiry differ. Quorum expires at head; classic also handles applicable policy-change cases. Short expired messages behind long-lived messages need not be promptly dead-lettered.

sources.title: RabbitMQ prefetch
sources.verification: RabbitMQ per-consumer QoS differs from channel-global interpretation; prefetch counts unacknowledged deliveries, not worker count.

sources.title: RabbitMQ Java client API
sources.verification: Client recovery does not recover application transaction responsibility; channel/thread ownership and callback behavior matter. Reviewed conceptual recovery discussion without claiming a local execution.

sources.title: RabbitMQ Java client 5.26.0 TLS source
sources.verification: Verified permissive TLS convenience overload and explicit SSLContext route. Retain peer-trust plus hostname-verification requirement; removed implication that a displayed runnable sample exists.

sources.title: Historical delayed plugin
sources.verification: Official repository states maintenance ended and Mnesia removal in 4.3 prevents carrying the old plugin forward. Its 4.4 native-delay note is not imported as a 4.3 capability.

sources.title: Spring AMQP 2.3.11
sources.verification: Correlated returned message is set before confirmation future with unique correlation identity and both mechanisms enabled. Framework semantics remain separate from direct Java-client behavior.

sources.title: RocketMQ 4.x PushConsumer
sources.verification: Traditional broadcasting delivers full messages per instance; cluster mode distributes work. Consumption retry is documented for cluster mode, not broadcast mode.

sources.title: RocketMQ 5.0 load balancing
sources.verification: 5.0 describes independent groups and within-group balancing; new PushConsumer and SimpleConsumer use message-based balancing. This differs from traditional queue assignment and broadcast API.

sources.title: RocketMQ 5.0 FIFO
sources.verification: Message group identifies FIFO unit; ordering prerequisites include a single producer and serial sends. Same business key alone cannot order concurrent producers.

sources.title: RocketMQ 5.0 delay
sources.verification: Documented timestamp model uses millisecond Unix time, default 24-hour range and 1000ms granularity; outside/past time may be immediately delivered. Delay topic type and arrival bursts matter. These are scoped document defaults, not all 5.x deployments.

sources.title: RocketMQ 5.0 retry
sources.verification: Push and Simple consumer retry state machines differ; Simple consumer uses InvisibleDuration. Retry policy is not a global exactly-once business execution counter.

sources.title: RocketMQ 5.0 transaction message
sources.verification: Half message precedes local transaction; persisted result supports checking. Guarantee is eventual producer-local/message consistency, not downstream global ACID. Documented timeout may roll back unresolved half messages.

sources.title: RocketMQ 4.9.8 transaction source
sources.verification: Verified UNKNOW enum usage and SEND_OK branch invoking local callback; flush disk/slave timeout and unavailable slave branches choose half-message rollback. This cannot cover a DB transaction committed before calling this protocol.

sources.title: Redis Pub/Sub
sources.verification: Pub/Sub at-most-once/offline loss is distinct from Streams recovery, retained in product comparison.

sources.title: Redis XAUTOCLAIM
sources.verification: Available since Redis 6.2; claims pending deliveries and does not guarantee external business effects exactly once.

sources.title: Guava EventBus
sources.verification: Official guidance does not recommend EventBus for new designs; in-process dispatch does not supply durable cross-process broker semantics.

sources.title: Cloudflare Queues retries
sources.verification: Explicit per-message ACK/retry and batch failure differ; exhausted retries require configured DLQ to retain failed work. Retained alternative with own contract, not imported into Kafka/RabbitMQ.
